evals.name: poc-scope-build-harvest
evals.prompt: Let's PoC this — I want to prove the executor can drive a sandboxed agent end-to-end before we plan anything. Can we scaffold something quick and see?
evals.expected_output: Opens by naming the single question ("can the executor drive a sandboxed agent end-to-end?") and the run-X-see-Y demonstration that would answer it — one or two lines, no PRD/TDD/plan. Declares quality bars suspended and sandboxes the work (scratch branch or spike/ dir). Builds the smallest thing that answers the question, hardcoding what isn't the question. Runs the demonstration and states a plain verdict (proven/disproven/unresolved). Then runs the mandatory harvest: writes docs/better-planning/research/<topic>-findings.md with the question, verdict + evidence, implications, code-worth-keeping paths, and dead ends; feeds the brief's Evidence section if a brief exists. Offers the next planning phase with the findings as input; does not merge spike code to main.
files: fixtures/taskpilot — greenfield-ish repo with an executor package and no planning space for this topic
assertions: one-question-scoped: the spike opens with a single named question and its run-X-see-Y answer condition
no-ladder-artifacts: no brief/PRD/TDD/plan/tasks are written for the spike itself
quality-bars-suspended-explicitly: the disposable-code trade is stated up front, and the work is sandboxed (branch or spike dir)
plain-verdict: the demonstration runs and the verdict is stated as proven/disproven/unresolved without spin
harvest-written: a research findings doc captures question, verdict, evidence, implications, keeper paths, and dead ends
no-wholesale-merge: spike code is kept as reference for later promotion, not merged to main

evals.name: harvest-a-finished-spike-before-moving-on
evals.prompt: Ok this was a spike PoC and I think we're done with it. What have we proven with this, what is still left? Let's make sure we don't lose the insights before we start the real repo.
evals.expected_output: Treats this as the harvest step of an existing spike: reconstructs the question(s) the spike was answering from the code and session, states verdicts with evidence (what ran, what it showed), and writes the findings doc under docs/better-planning/research/ — proven/disproven/unresolved, implications for planning, which code artifacts are worth carrying forward (as reference), and dead ends worth remembering. Distinguishes proven from merely built. Updates/creates the brief's Evidence section. Recommends the onward route (e.g. brainstorm or PRD in the new repo, citing the findings doc) rather than migrating spike code wholesale.
files: fixtures/taskpilot — a scratch repo containing a working but messy end-to-end PoC and no documentation of what it demonstrated
assertions: verdicts-with-evidence: each thing 'proven' is tied to an actual demonstrated run, and unproven-but-built parts are labelled as such
findings-doc-created: the harvest lands in docs/better-planning/research/ with implications, keeper paths, and dead ends
insights-fed-upstream: the brief/Evidence trail is updated or created so planning starts from the findings
onward-route-not-migration: the recommendation is to plan from the evidence and rebuild keepers properly, not to carry the spike code over wholesale
